resources.title: People, places and objects to respect;
resources.description: Theme: NATIONAL CONSCIOUSNESS | Sub-theme: NATIONAL CONSCIOUSNESS | Content: 1. Meaning of Respect: a) Feeling of admiration for something or somebody because of their good qualities or achievement. b) polite behaviour towards or care for somebody/ thing/place you think is important. 2. People to Respect: Traditional rulers, Parents, Leaders e.g. prefects, principals, Ministers, Commissioners etc,; Politicians, Religious leaders. 3. Place/things To Respect: Time, Public properties Constitution, Mace, Public building, National flags, Palaces, and utilities. 4. Respecting people e.g. greetings, running errands, respecting things e.g. standing for the national Anthem
resources.objectives: Pupil should be able to: 1. define respect; 2. identify people, places and things to respect; 3. demonstrate ways of respecting people, places and things.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Tells pupils stories why we should respect elders and leaders. 2. Demonstrates how they can show respect in their localities. 3. Shows pupils charts and pictures of a mosque, church, palace flag, shield, mace and the Nigerian Constitution, etc.

Students: 1. Listen to the stories and participate in class discussion. 2. Look and interpret the pictures and regalia. 3. Listen and ask questions. 4. Demonstrate how to respect: people, places, things and time.
resources.resources: 1. Charts of children greeting their elders in their localities. 2. Charts and pictures of Mosque, Church and Palace, etc. 3. Pictures of Government properties. 4. cartoons, textbooks, posters, Video dips. 5. Visit to important. places e.g. a kings palace, mosque, church, museum, National Assembly
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. define the concept of respect; 2. mention places or objects that should be respected; 3. mention two reasons why we should respect elders, parents, teachers, staff, religious and political leaders; 4. demonstrate how to show respect for people, places and things.

resources.title: Rules and Regulations in the Society
resources.description: Theme: GOOD SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR | Sub-theme: GOOD SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR | Content: 1. Meaning of rules and regulations - do's and don'ts that guide social behaviour. 2. Gains of obeying rules and regulations e.g. love by elders, Gifts from elders and friends, Praise, etc. 3. Results of disobeying rules and regulations e.g. unhappiness, punishment, denial of privileges such as food, playing with mates, etc.; rejection by loved ones 4. NAFDAC laws and Regulations on Food and Drugs Control e.g. Quality Control laws; Laws on sale and use of foods, medicines and cosmetics; Laboratory Laws; Product Registration laws; Importation Laws, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of rules and regulations; 2. mention some of the gains of obeying rules and regulations; 3. mention the results of disobeying rules and regulations; 4. mention the rules and regulations for food and drug administration.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads class discussion on the meaning of rules and Regulations. 2. Shows pictures/video clips of children receiving gifts and guides discussion on the various gains for obeying rules. 3. Presents pictures of children suffering from the results of disobeying rules and regulations and leads class discussion on the pictures. 4. Discusses the NAFDAC rules and regulations on food and drug control.

Students: 1. Participate in class discussion on rules and regulations. 2. Interpret the pictures on children receiving gifts and participate in discussion. 3. Describe pictures of children suffering from the results of disobeying laws.
resources.resources: 1. Pupils' text book 2. Pictures of children receiving gifts. 3. Video clips 4. Pictures of children suffering from the consequences of disobedience 5. Food and Drug packs and instructional leaflets. 6. Pictures and Diagrams of different foods and Drugs.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. say what they are expected to do and not to do in their community; 2. mention gains of obeying rules and regulations; 3. mention results of disobeying rules and regulations. 4. mention three rules and regulations of NAFDAC on foods and drugs control.

resources.title: Importance of Civic Education
resources.description: Theme: CIVIC EDUCATION | Sub-theme: CIVIC EDUCATION | Content: 1. Why study Civic Education: - understand democratic and Civic rights and responsibilities. - nurture and sustain democracy, etc. 2. Topics and Importance of Civic Education: - learn about systems and institution of government, democratic processes, etc. - acquire skills such as active citizenship, inquiry, cooperation, etc. - stimulation of civic engagement in the political, social and economic processes. - citizens are educated on their multiple roles in society, e.g. as producers and consumers, of goods and services etc. 3. Public Health Enlightenment Campaigns on: - HIV/AIDS Education, - Drug Abuse Education, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. discuss the need for Civic Education in Nigeria; 2. mention the topics learnt in Civic Education and their importance; 3. identify some public health enlightenment campaigns as part of civic education.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides discussion on the need for Civic Education. 2. Leads pupils to mention the topics and specific benefits of learning Civic Education. 3. Guides the class to identify some ways of public health enlightenment campaigns as part of civic education.

Students: 1. Listen to teacher’s explanations. 2. Contribute to discussions. 3. Identify ways of public health enlightenment campaigns as part of Civic Education.
resources.resources: 1. Textbooks 2. Pictures of a democratic activity and citizens performing some Civic responsibilities in a democracy e.g. senate in session and people voting and campaign. 3. Video clips on democratic activities. 4. Radio Jingles 5. Video Clips, Posters and Pictures of Public Health Enlightenment Campaigns.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. say why it is important to learn Civic Education in Nigeria; 2. enumerate three benefits derivable from studying Civic Education. 3. mention any two public health awareness campaigns.

resources.title: Meaning of Social Studies
resources.description: Theme: FUNDAMENTAL OF SOCIAL STUDIES | Sub-theme: FUNDAMENTAL OF SOCIAL STUDIES | Content: Meaning of social studies: The study of man and how his problems are solved in the environment.
resources.objectives: Pupil should be able to explain the meaning of social studies.
resources.activities:
Teacher: Explains and guides the pupil to explain the meaning of social studies.

Students: Listen and respond to questions in class on the meaning of social studies.
resources.resources: Pupils’ text and work book.
resources.assessment: Pupil to explain the meaning of social studies.

resources.title: The Family
resources.description: Theme: FAMILY AS THE BASIC UNIT OF SOCIETY | Sub-theme: FUNDAMENTAL OF SOCIAL STUDIES | Content: 1. Meaning of a family (father, mother, and children). 2. Types of family - The Nuclear Family: father, mother and children. - Extended Family: father, mother children, grandfather and grandmother, uncles, aunts, cousins and nephews.
resources.objectives: The pupils should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of family; 2. identify types of family 3. explain types of family;
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads pupils to find out the meaning of the word family and through guided questions explains the types of family. 2. Leads pupils to identify types of family.

Students: 1. Find out from home the meaning of the word “family” and report back to class. 2. Listen and respond to questions in class.
resources.resources: 1. Pupils text books. 2. Family photographs cartoons, video CDs ROMs, etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. explain the meaning of the word “family”; 2. mention 2 types of family; 3. explain types of family.

resources.title: Qualities of a good family
resources.description: Theme: FAMILY AS THE BASIC UNIT OF SOCIETY | Sub-theme: FUNDAMENTAL OF SOCIAL STUDIES | Content: 1. Qualities of a good family: honesty, contentment, interest of others, not greedy, not selfish, discipline, obedience, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. state the qualities of a good family.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides pupils to identify and explain qualities of a good family.

Students: 1. Role play the family showing the qualities of a good family e.g. honesty, love, caring, etc.
resources.resources: Pictures and Charts showing moral values as honesty, contentment, obedience, discipline etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: mention 3 qualities of a good family.

resources.title: Meaning and Types of Culture
resources.description: Theme: CULTURE AND SOCIAL VALUES | Sub-theme: FUNDAMENTAL OF SOCIAL STUDIES | Content: 1. Meaning of culture e.g. peoples’ ways of life that include dressing, dancing, eating, etc. 2. Types of culture e.g. material, non-material.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of culture; 2. list types of culture;
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Through guided questions and role play, leads the pupils to understand the meaning of the word “culture”. 2. Leads pupil to outline types of culture.

Students: 1. Listen and respond to questions in class and participate in role play. 2. Outline and write types of culture.
resources.resources: 1. Pictures of people wearing traditional dresses. 2. Pictures showing material, and non-material culture.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. state the meaning of culture; 2. explain types of culture.

resources.title: Values that Show Good Morals in Our Society
resources.description: Theme: CULTURE AND SOCIAL VALUES | Sub-theme: FUNDAMENTAL OF SOCIAL STUDIES | Content: Examples of morals to show what is right i.e. greeting, respect, loyalty, kindness, honesty, contentment, tolerance, etc. and what is wrong, e.g. stealing, bullying, fighting, lying etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. explain values which show morals e.g. what is right and what is wrong.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads pupils to identify values which show morals in the society and attitudes that are wrong.

Students: 1. Demonstrate different types of good and bad values.
resources.resources: 1. Cartoons, posters, ROM film and video clips, regalia, photographs, exhibit etc.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. explain values which are considered right and wrong.

resources.title: Reasons for Taking Substances into the Body
resources.description: Theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Sub-theme: FUNDAMENTAL OF SOCIAL STUDIES | Content: 1. Reasons for taking substances into the body: - stay alive, - hunger, - thirst, - enjoyment, - imitation, - curiosity, - availability, etc. 2. Effects of taking substances into the body e.g. stomach pain, vomiting, stooling, sleeplessness or restlessness, dullness, dizziness, nausea, fainting, death, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. give reasons for taking substances into the body; 2. mention the effect of taking substances into the body.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Calls on the pupils to demonstrate each of the reasons. 2. Dramatize by showing the reasons for taking substances into the body. 3. Uses stories; to highlight effects of taking substances into the body. 4. Asks pupils to narrate their experiences of taking substances into the body.

Students: 1. Demonstrate and dramatize the reasons. 2. Listen to the teacher’s stories and make comments. 3. Narrate their own experiences of taking substances into the body.
resources.resources: 1. Posters, charts and pictures of the reasons. 2. Charts, pictures, posters and drawing materials.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. give reasons for taking substances into the body; 2. mention 4 effects of taking substances into the body.

resources.title: Overdose (too much eating, drinking or smoking)
resources.description: Theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Sub-theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Content: Causes and Observable signs/ symptoms of overdose: e.g. coughing incessantly, fainting, stooling, etc. Effects of too much eating and drinking: - Frequent urinating, bed wetting, intoxication, etc. - Watery eyes, coughing, chocking fainting, dizziness, - Loss of memory, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. demonstrate the looks and behaviours of people who take too much food, drink or smoke; 2. mention the effects of drinking too much; 3. mention the effects of inhaling too much;
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Presents drawings and paintings of sad faces, protruding stomach to emphasize the effects of drinking too much. 2. Asks pupils to narrate their own experiences. 3. Shows drawings and paintings of sad faces. 4. Shows pictures of people exhibiting these symptoms or signs.

Students: 1. Study pictures shown by the teacher. 2. Narrate own experiences. 3. Copy drawing and painting. 4. Demonstrate the behaviours and looks shown in the pictures. 5. Suggest what should be done. 6. Dramatize the suggestions.
resources.resources: 1. Charts, pictures, posters and drawing materials. 2. Charts, pictures, posters and drawing materials 3. Pictures and Charts 4. Posters of children helping sufferers.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. mention the effects of drinking too much; 2. mention 3 effects of inhaling too much; 3. demonstrate the behaviours and looks of people who eat, drink and smoke too much;

resources.title: Food
resources.description: Theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Sub-theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Content: 1. Meaning of food. “Food is anything we eat, drink or take into our body to give us energy and help us grow”. 2. Foods eaten in the locality (bread, eggs, yam, garri, fish, meat, tuwo etc). 3. Sources of food in the locality/farms, markets, rivers, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. define food; 2. mention some of the foods eaten in their locality; 3. mention the sources of food in the community.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Asks pupils to bring samples of these food items from homes. 2. Asks them to identify the food they brought from home. 3. Asks pupils to find out from home the sources of food they eat. 4. Asks pupils to paint any of the food items mentioned.

Students: 1. Bring food items from homes and participate in identifying the food items. 2. Participate in the discussion on meaning of food. 3. Find out from home sources of food in their locality. 4. Paint any of the food items mentioned.
resources.resources: 1. Real food items. 2. Picture of foods. 3. Video Clips on food. 4. Pictures of farms and markets where food items are produced, sold and bought.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. define food; 2. mention 5 of the foods eaten in the locality. 3. mention the sources of food in the community.

resources.title: Food Safety
resources.description: Theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Sub-theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Content: 1. Meaning of Food Safety:  How to ensure that what we eat, drink or take into our body is not harmful to health. 2. Guide to Food Safety:  Reading food Labels;  Observe signs of food spoilage and causative organisms;  Washing hands before and after food preparation, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. define food safety; 2. mention ways of ensuring food safety.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads pupils to define food safety. 2. Asks questions to lead pupils to identify ways of making sure that food is safe.

Students: 1. Define food safety. 2. Participate in mentioning ways of ensuring food safety.
resources.resources: 1. Pupils Textbooks. 2. Pictures showing different ways of making food safe.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. define food safety; 2. mention ways of ensuring food safety.

resources.title: Risk Factors in Food.
resources.description: Theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Sub-theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Content: 1. Meaning of Risk Factors: “Those factors that drive the occurrence of a hazard”. 2. Examples of Risk Factors in Food:  Adulteration  Food fraud incidences  Agro-chemical induced death, etc. 3. Risk Factors in Food distribution and Preparation:  Poor storage conditions;  Poor handling:  Poor Hygiene;  Other Unknown Risks.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. explain risk factors; 2. state risk factors in food; 3. identify risk factors in food distribution and preparation.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads pupils to identify and explain risk factors. 2. Presents pictures /photographs of risk factors in food distribution and preparation. 3. Guides pupils to state risk factors in food distribution and preparation.

Students: 1. Explain risk factors. 2. Participate in class discussion on risk factors associated with food distribution and preparation. 3. Ask and answer questions.
resources.resources: 1. Pupils Textbooks. 2. Video clips on risk factors in food. 3. Pictures /photographs of risk factors in food distribution and preparation
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. explain risk factors; 2. state risk factors in food; 3. identify risk factors associated with food distribution and preparation.

resources.title: Sources and Uses of Water
resources.description: Theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Sub-theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Content: 1. Sources of water supply in the locality:  Stream  Spring  River  Tap  Bore-hole  Rainfall,  Well etc. 2. Uses of water:  Drinking;  Washing;  Cooking, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. mention sources of water supply in the locality; 2. enumerate the uses of water in homes.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads pupils to discuss sources of water supply. 2. Uses pictures and questions to guide pupils in enumerating the sources of water in homes.

Students: 1. Participate in discussion. 2. Interpret the pictures. 3. Enumerate the sources and uses of water supply in homes.
resources.resources: 1. Pictures depicting sources of water supply. 2. Pictures showing domestic uses of water.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. mention 4 sources of water supply in the locality. 2. enumerate 3 uses of water in homes.

resources.title: Concept of Security
resources.description: Theme: ELEMENTS OF SECURITY | Sub-theme: ELEMENTS OF SECURITY | Content: 1. Meaning of security of life and property.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Explain the meaning of security. 2. Take precautions against dangers.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides pupils to explain the meaning of security. 2. Guides pupils to identify sources of danger and insecurity.

Students: 1. Contribute ideas to the meaning of security. 2. Find out other sources of insecurity.
resources.resources: Textbooks, pictures on road accidents and fire outbreaks.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. explain the meaning of security.

resources.title: Importance of Civic Education
resources.description: Theme: CIVIC EDUCATION | Sub-theme: CIVIC EDUCATION | Content: 1. Why study Civic Education: - understand democratic and Civic rights and responsibilities. - nurture and sustain democracy. 2. Importance of Civic Education to national development e.g. learn about systems and institution of government, democratic processes, etc. - acquire skills such as active citizenship, inquiry, cooperation, etc. 3. Stimulation of civic engagement in the political, social and economic processes. - citizens are educated on their multiple roles in society, e.g. as producers and consumers, of goods and services etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. discuss the need for Civic Education in Nigeria; 2. analyze the importance of Civic Education to National development.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads pupils to recall the meaning of Civic Education. 2. Discusses the need for Civic Education with Pupils. 3. Leads pupils to identify the specific benefits of having Civic Education.

Students: 1. Listen to teacher's explanations. 2. Contribute to discussions. 3. Write notes.
resources.resources: 1. Textbooks 2. Pictures of a democratic activity and citizens performing some civic responsibilities in a democracy e.g. senate in session and people voting and campaign. 3. Video clips on democratic activities.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. explain the need for Civic Education in Nigeria; 2. enumerate three benefits derivable from studying Civic Education.

resources.title: Meaning and types of Community
resources.description: Theme: OUR COMMUNITY | Sub-theme: OUR COMMUNITY | Content: 1. Meaning of Community (a collection of a group of people in a given place) 2. Types of community - traditional communities town and villages - modern communities/ institutions e.g. school community. 3. Members of Communities e.g. father, mother, siblings, uncles, aunties, community leaders etc. 4. Rules in the Community: - obedience - orderliness - cooperation - respect - loyalty - peaceful existence - sanitation - honesty/sincerity 5. Roles of member of community includes: - Community development - cooperation - payment taxes and dues - Training the young ones - Taken part in communal work.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of community; 2. mention types of community; 3. mention members of the community; 4. rules in the Community. 5. identify roles of members of community.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the meaning of community. 2. Identifies three rules in the community. 3. Asks pupils to find out from their parents the rules in their community and report back to the class. 4. Explain each responsibility and how to carry it out,

Students: 1. Learns the rules as identified by the teacher. 2. Find out from their parent rules in their community and report back to the class. 3. Listen to explanation and ask questions,
resources.resources: 1. Pupils' textbooks. 2. Pictures. 3. Charts 4. Video clips 5. Drama of different communities Members of the class.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. explain the meaning of community; 2. differentiate between traditional and modern types of communities; 3. identify members that constitute a community; 4. list at least five rules in the community. 5. mention some of the responsibilities of members in a community,

resources.title: Leaders in our Community
resources.description: Theme: OUR COMMUNITY | Sub-theme: OUR COMMUNITY | Content: 1. The idea of community leadership in Nigerian traditional settings e.g.:  Yoruba - Oba  Hausa - Sarld  Igbo - Eze  Benin - Enoge  Nupe - Etsu  Ebira - Ohinoyi, etc  Other title holders in the community. 2. Duties of community leaders e.g.:  settlement of disputes  ensuring peace  organizing community work  link between government and the community, etc. 3. Qualities of community leaders: caring, intelligent, wise, patient, integrity, courage, honest, etc. 4. Appreciation and reward e.g. gifts, visitation cooperation, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. name some community leaders in the locality; 2. mention duties of community leaders; 3.. mention the qualities of community leaders; 4. show how to appreciate and reward community leaders. 5. explain the responsibilities of community members,
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Creates discussion that leads the pupils to identify community heads. 2. Asks questions that lead pupils to suggest the roles of community leaders. 3. Invites resource persons to talk about their roles. 4. Guides pupils to mention the qualities of community leaders and show how to appreciate and reward them.

Students: 1. Participate in the discussion to identify community leaders. 2. Listen to resource persons and ask questions. 3. Mention the qualities of community leaders and how to appreciate and reward them.
resources.resources: 1. Pupils text book 2. Pictures of community leaders in their locality 3. Gifts 4. Video clips of award ceremonies 5. Monuments created in honour of some community leaders.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. name some community leaders in their locality; 2. mention at least three roles of community leaders; 3. mention the qualities and how to appreciate and reward community leaders.

resources.title: Scope of Social Studies
resources.description: Theme: FUNDAMENTALS OF SOCIAL STUDIES | Sub-theme: OUR COMMUNITY | Content: 1. Meaning of scope of social studies:  The areas which social studies focuses to solve man’s problems of solver.  Areas which social studies focuses are:  Critical thinking  Reflective thinking  Problem solving.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Explain ‘scope of social studies’. 2. Identify areas of focus in social studies.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guide pupils to explain the scope of social studies. 2. Guide pupils to identify areas of focus in social studies.

Students: 1. Find out from home how family takes its social and economic decisions such as association to join and food to eat.
resources.resources: 1. Pupils’ textbooks and video clips on how decisions are taken to solve problem.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. explain scope of social studies. 2. Identify areas of focus in social studies.

resources.title: Physical Environment
resources.description: Theme: FUNDMENTALS OF SOCIAL STUDIES | Sub-theme: OUR COMMUNITY | Content: 1. Our physical environment:  Some people live in desert condition  Other live in fertile places  Some near lakes, rivers or oceans  Some in mountains  Other low laying areas  Climate varies tremendously over the globe.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify our different physical environment.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads the pupils to discover our different physical environment.

Students: 1. Participant in class discussion. 2. Respond to the teacher’s questions.
resources.resources: 1. Pupils textbooks 2. Pictures showing different environment 3. Video clips.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify our different physical environment.

resources.title: Foods We Eat in our Culture as Family Members.
resources.description: Theme: FAMILY AS THE BASIC UNIT OF SOCIETY | Sub-theme: OUR COMMUNITY | Content: 1. Some Nigerian foods are; Yam, Eba, Amala, Tuwo Shinkafa, Plantain, Rice, Beans, Cocoyam, Pounded Yam, Akpu, Starch etc. 2. Consequences of Eating together as a family: e.g. promotes communalism, Happiness, family unity and loyalty, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to; 1. List types of food in the Nigerian Culture. 2. Mention reasons why we eat together.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Uses guided questions to lead pupils to name the various foods we eat in our culture. 2. Asks the pupils to mention reasons why we eat together.

Students: 1. Participate in the discussion on the types of food. 2. Respond to teacher’s questions on the types of food.
resources.resources: 1. Pupils’ text and workbooks. 2. Picture showing different types of food in our culture. 3. Picture of happy moods of people eating together in the family.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. state 2 types of food eaten in their homes. 2. state reasons why we eat together.

resources.title: Importance of these Foods to our Growth
resources.description: Theme: FAMILY AS THE BAISC UNIT OF SOCIETY | Sub-theme: OUR COMMUNITY | Content: 1. The Nutrients in the food we take are: - Carbohydrate - Protein - Vitamins - Fats and Oil. 2. Importance of food to our growth: - supply energy - build our body - Keep the body healthy - provide heats and energy.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to list: 1. The nutrients in the foods we take. 2. Mention the importance of food to our growth.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads the pupils through guided questions to say the nutrients we get from different foods e.g.:  carbohydrate (Yam/ bread)  Protein (Meat/fish/egg)  Vitamins (Fruits/ vegetables  Fats and oil (Butter/ cheese), etc. 2. Guides the pupils to identify the functions of the nutrients food we take;  Carbohydrate supplies energy to the body  Protein to build our body  Vitamin to keep our body healthy  Fast and oil to provide heat and energy.

Students: 1. Draw different types of food and say the importance to growth. 2. Respond to the teacher’s questions on the topic.
resources.resources: 1. Pupils’ textbook. 2. Pictures showing groups of food and their nutrients. 3. Real objects of food from their locality.
resources.assessment: Pupils to; 1. list 3 types of Nigerian foods and identify the nutrients in the listed foods. 2. mention the importance of food to our growth.

resources.title: Greetings and Respect to Elders in our Culture
resources.description: Theme: CULTURE AND BASIC VALUES | Sub-theme: OUR COMMUNITY | Content: 1. Greeting is a way of showing respect to people and appreciating them. 2. Forms of greeting include: kneeling, prostrating, shaking of hands, clenching of fists etc. 3. Greetings promote tolerance, good neighborliness, Courtesy, friendliness etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Recognize greetings as a way of showing respect. 2. Perform various acts of greetings in their locality. 3. Recognize the importance of greetings.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides pupils through questioning to list ways of greeting in their locality. 2. Demonstrates the various ways of greeting in our Culture.

Students: 1. Find out more ways of greetings in our culture. 2. Draw different ways of greetings they can identify.
resources.resources: 1. Pictures of different ways of greeting. 2. Video clips
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. explain the meaning of greetings 2. list different ways of greetings from different cultures in Nigeria; 3. mention some of the importance of greeting in our community.

resources.title: Keeping our Environment Clean
resources.description: Theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Sub-theme: OUR COMMUNITY | Content: Ways of keeping our environment clean:  Proper disposal of waste.  Proper use of the toilets/urinary:  Provision of waste bins.  Allowing drains to flow.  Clearing and sweeping round our surroundings.  Regular sweeping of our homes.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. mention ways of keeping our environment clean.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Asks questions to lead pupils to suggest ways of keeping our environment clean. 2. Gets the pupils practically involved in different ways of keeping their environment clean.

Students: 1. Respond to teacher’s questions on the ways to keep our environment clean. 2. Demonstrate involvement in acts of keeping the environment clean.
resources.resources: 1. Pictures showing clean and dirty environment. 2. Cleaning tools
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. mention 3 ways of keeping our environment clean. 2. Mention some of the tools needed for carrying out different cleaning activities.

resources.title: Accidents in the School/Home
resources.description: Theme: SOCIAL AND HEALTH ISSUES | Sub-theme: OUR COMMUNITY | Content: 1. Meaning of Accidents: “Accidents are unplanned events that lead to injury, Damage or death”. 2. Causes of accidents in school and Home. 3. Prevention of Accidents in the school/ home:  Remove all dangerous objects from the surroundings.  Do not play with dangerous or sharp objects.  Avoid exposed electricity sources (naked wires).  Removing what has caused the accident.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of accidents; 2. identify causes of home and school accidents; 3. mention ways of preventing accidents in school/home.
resources.activities:
Teacher: Uses guided questions to: 1. explain the meaning of accidents; 2. identify causes of accidents in the school and home; 3. state ways of preventing accidents around the school/ home.

Students: 1. Respond to the teacher’s questions. 2. Participate in class discussion. 3. Demonstrate how to avoid accidents.
resources.resources: 1. Pupils’ textbooks 2. Pictures showing dangerous and sharp objects. 3. Video clips.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. explain the meaning of accidents; 2. identify causes of home and school accidents; 3. mention 3 ways we can avoid accidents in the school and at home.

resources.title: Drugs

resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. explain the meaning of harmful substances. 2. give 2 examples of harmful substances. 3. mention 2 ways of preventing intake of harmful substances.

resources.description: Theme: NATIONAL CONSCIOUSNESS | Sub-theme: NATIONAL CONSCIOUSNESS | Content: 1. Reasons for patriotism:  to promote unity  to promote development  to ensure full and proper use of resources  to help the nation benefit from our knowledge and skills.

Description of National symbols:  the eagle in the Nigerian coat of arms represents strength,  the green colour of the national flag stands for agriculture, and white stands for peace, etc. 3. Differentiation: e.g.  National symbols- national flag, currency, National Anthem, Coat of Arms, Constitution, etc.  other symbols: . · traditional leaders; · religious leaders and highway codes; etc. 4.
